signature: ESP32-S3, IP5306, CP2102, microSD, 2.8in ILI9341 TFT, buttons, buzzer, 4x WS2812, external antenna
summary: ESP32-DIV v2 core board components.
source_span: - **ESP32-S3** The main microcontroller. Fixes previous pin conflicts, improves USB support, and allows future expansions. - **IP5306 Power Management IC** Manages battery charging and boost conversion, providing stable operation under load. - **Battery Voltage Divider** Monitors battery voltage. - **CP2102 USB-to-Serial Converter** Handles firmware flashing and serial communication. - **SD Card Slot** Stores logs, scripts, and configurations. - **ILI9341 TFT Display (2.8")** Main interface display. - **Soft Tactile Buttons** Reliable low-profile switches for user interaction. - **Buzzer** Optional audio feedback. - **4× WS2812 NeoPixels** Visual status indicators. - **External Antenna Connector** Supports flexible antenna setups for improved range.

signature: 3x NRF24 (2.4GHz), CC1101 (SubGHz), IR tx/rx, replaceable; pogo-pin shield interface
summary: ESP32-DIV v2 shield board components, connected to the core board by pogo pins.
source_span: - **3 × NRF24 Modules** – Dedicated for 2.4GHz operations. - **CC1101 Sub-GHz Transceiver** – For Sub-GHz connectivity. - **Multiple Antennas** – Separate antennas for different bands. - **Infrared Circuitry** – For IR input/output operations. ### 🧩 Shield Interface ESP32-DIV v2 uses **pogo-pin headers** for shield connection: - Thin stacking without bulky connectors - Clean electrical contact - Easy shield replacement and expansion

signature: v2: gpio_reset_pin(SCK,MISO,MOSI,CS); SPI.begin(12,13,11,10); SPI mode0 MSB first 4MHz; SD.begin(10, SPI, 4000000); pinMode(38,INPUT_PULLUP)
summary: How the stock firmware mounts the microSD on DIV v2 (ESP32-S3): explicit SPI.begin with the SD pins, mode 0, 4 MHz, SD.begin with the SPI object and 4 MHz.
source_span: void sdSpiInit() { #if defined(SD_SCLK) && defined(SD_MISO) && defined(SD_MOSI) && defined(SD_CS) #if TOUCH_SHARES_TFT_SPI s_sdSpi.begin(SD_SCLK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS); #else // On ESP32-S3 (v2), RFID bitbang remaps these pins — reset before reclaim. // On classic ESP32 (v1), SD often shares SPI with TFT_eSPI; gpio_reset_pin // after tft.init() can WDT/reboot during boot SD mount. #if BOARD_HAS_ESP32S3 gpio_reset_pin((gpio_num_t)SD_SCLK); gpio_reset_pin((gpio_num_t)SD_MISO); gpio_reset_pin((gpio_num_t)SD_MOSI); gpio_reset_pin((gpio_num_t)SD_CS); #endif SPI.begin(SD_SCLK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS); SPI.setDataMode(SPI_MODE0); SPI.setBitOrder(MSBFIRST); SPI.setFrequency(4000000); #endif #endif } bool sdMountChipSelect(uint8_t cs) { #if TOUCH_SHARES_TFT_SPI return SD.begin(cs, s_sdSpi, 4000000); #else return SD.begin(cs, SPI, 4000000);
constraints: Source: ESP32-DIV firmware utils.cpp (sdSpiInit/sdMountChipSelect) at the pinned commit; v2 has TOUCH_SHARES_TFT_SPI=0 so the default SPI object is used.
Before calling SPI.begin, v2 (BOARD_HAS_ESP32S3) first gpio_reset_pin()s SCK/MISO/MOSI/CS because the RFID bit-bang code remaps them.
Stock code mounts via SD.begin(cs, SPI, 4000000) where cs=SD_CS=10; calling SD.begin(10) alone on the core's default SPI pins and clock is not what the firmware does.

signature: before SD use drive HIGH: SD_CS(10), CC1101_CS(5), PN532_SS, CSN_PIN_1(4), CSN_PIN_2(48), CSN_PIN_3(21); CE_PIN_3(14)=LOW
summary: The SD bus is shared, so every other SPI slave's chip-select is pinMode(OUTPUT)+digitalWrite(HIGH) before mounting or using the card, so none holds MISO.
source_span: /** Deselect every other SPI slave that shares the SD bus so none holds MISO. */ static void sdRaiseCsPin(int pin) { if (pin < 0) { return; } pinMode(pin, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(pin, HIGH); } static void sdReleaseOtherChipSelects() { #if defined(CC1101_CS) sdRaiseCsPin(CC1101_CS); #endif #if defined(PN532_SS) sdRaiseCsPin(PN532_SS); #endif #if defined(CSN_PIN_1) sdRaiseCsPin(CSN_PIN_1); #endif #if defined(CSN_PIN_2) sdRaiseCsPin(CSN_PIN_2); #endif #if defined(CSN_PIN_3) sdRaiseCsPin(CSN_PIN_3); #endif // Scanner bit-bangs CE/CSN on these pins; keep CE low / CSN high after leaving. #if defined(CE_PIN_3) pinMode(CE_PIN_3, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(CE_PIN_3, LOW);
constraints: Per the pinned v2 pin definitions: CC1101_CS=5, PN532_SS=5 (wiki says 4), CSN_PIN_1=4, CSN_PIN_2=48, CSN_PIN_3=21, CE_PIN_3=14.
Derived failure mode (not stated in the source): if these lines float or sit low, the card can answer the initial handshake and mount, yet later writes fail.

signature: after SD.begin(): SPI.setFrequency(4000000); keep SPI pinmux; do not SPI.end() while CC1101/nRF24 need the bus
summary: Remounting SD on the shared bus: raise other CS lines, SPI.begin with the SD pins, mode 0, SD.end(), SD.begin; then restore 4 MHz because SD.begin leaves the bus at 16-40 MHz which the CC1101 cannot use.
source_span: static bool sdRemountSoft() { sdReleaseOtherChipSelects(); #if defined(SD_SCLK) && defined(SD_MISO) && defined(SD_MOSI) && defined(SD_CS) #if TOUCH_SHARES_TFT_SPI s_sdSpi.begin(SD_SCLK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS); #else // Do not SPI.end()/gpio_reset here — that tears down CC1101 after SubGHz Init. SPI.begin(SD_SCLK, SD_MISO, SD_MOSI, SD_CS); SPI.setDataMode(SPI_MODE0); SPI.setBitOrder(MSBFIRST); #endif #endif SD.end(); s_sdFsMounted = false; delay(2); if (sdTryBeginOrder()) { s_sdFsMounted = true; #if !TOUCH_SHARES_TFT_SPI // SD.begin() often leaves the bus at 16–40 MHz; CC1101 cannot use that. SPI.setFrequency(4000000); #endif return true; } return false; }
constraints: Source: utils.cpp sdRemountSoft at the pinned commit.

source_span: 3. **Run the OTA Update** - Navigate to **Firmware Update** - Select **OTA Update** - Enter the firmware URL - Press **Update** - The device reboots automatically when done

signature: SD card FAT32, file named firmware.bin in root, menu: Firmware Update > SD Card Update
summary: Firmware update from an SD card.
source_span: 1. **Prepare the SD Card** - Format a microSD card to **FAT32** - Download the latest `.bin` file from the repository - Rename it to `firmware.bin` - Place it in the SD card **root directory** - Eject the card safely 2. **Insert the SD Card** - Power off the ESP32-DIV - Insert the SD card 3. **Run the SD Card Update** - Power on the device - Go to **Firmware Update** - Select **SD Card Update** - Select `firmware.bin` - Press **Update** - Device reboots after flashing
